superseded_by.note: the sha256 above is v3's, which this manifest recorded truthfully when it was written. It is NOT the digest of the file at that path today. It is left as recorded rather than refreshed, because a manifest that silently re-points at a newer artifact stops being a record of anything. The live binding is in the M11g manifest.

items.defect: the partition counted decisive censored-only pairs as supplied to fitting, while the contract declares exact-only pKi regression with MSE. Those pairs have a class label and no regression target, so nothing could have been fitted on them.
items.fix: three eligibilities are now kept apart: classification (decisive label, exact or censored), regression (exact-only median pKi, the established `pair_regression` rule), and validation-RMSE (regression-eligible AND status ok AND not discordant -- the endpoint's own eval rule, NOT reused from training eligibility).

default_config_membership_verified_uncha.why_the_digest_changed: the recorded fields changed -- two eligibility flags per pair instead of one -- not because any pair moved. Verified by comparing assignments pair by pair rather than assuming.

items.defect: build_partition accepted `fraction` and `seed` and then let iter_a_pairs use the module defaults, so a caller asking for a different split got the default one -- honoured in the record and ignored in the assignment.
items.fix: the configuration is threaded through every assignment path and validated.

items.defect: recurrence was defined against classification eligibility.
items.fix: recurrence is defined against the exact pair set the model-facing TRAINING loader emits, after eligibility and feature exclusions.

items.defect: feature coverage was checked once over the whole cohort and against the LOGICAL fingerprint width, which called every packed vector unusable.
items.fix: coverage is checked per entity role, against the STORED width, with missing and unusable counted apart and non-finite values rejected only where the dtype can hold one.

discordance_treatment.training: discordant pairs REMAIN available for training. M4 leaves them available and denies them only scoring standing (docs/M11.md §7a (h)); excluding them here would be a different rule than the endpoint declares.
discordance_treatment.validation_rmse: discordant pairs are EXCLUDED from checkpoint selection, because selection is an evaluation and the endpoint's own eval rule refuses them. Replicate exacts four logs apart cannot arbitrate which checkpoint is better.

eligibility.classification_rule: A-only status `ok` and label in {active, inactive}
eligibility.note: three different questions, kept apart. An earlier revision used the classification figure as 'supplied to fitting', which overcounted: the declared objective is exact-only pKi regression with MSE, so a decisive censored-only pair has a class label and no regression target.
eligibility.regression_rule: median of the pair's exact pKi values, the established `pair_regression` rule. Exact, positive, finite `=` records only; a censoring boundary is never substituted for a point.
eligibility.validation_rmse_rule: regression-eligible AND label status `ok` AND not discordant -- the endpoint's own `eval_excluded` rule. NOT derived from training eligibility: selecting checkpoints on pairs the endpoint refuses to score would pick a checkpoint on evidence that disagrees with itself.

feature_visibility.cache_identity_rule: A cache is identified by its spec AND its population. An extension cannot inherit the accepted cache's identity merely because the recipe is unchanged -- the store's own contract says a spec 'does not say which entities went in, so it cannot identify a cache on its own'. Any extension is registered under its own manifest and storage digests, and the experiment binds the artifacts actually loaded.
feature_visibility.correction: An earlier draft declared ALL features train_only. That was wrong: a fixed fingerprint and a frozen embedding are deterministic functions of a structure or a sequence and carry no label information, so computing them for an evaluation entity leaks nothing.

partition.assignment_method: blake2b-64 of (seed, inchikey, sequence_sha256), uniform in [0,1), validation if the draw is below the fraction
partition.scope: train and validation are both carved out of snapshot A
partition.whole_pairs_together: by construction -- the key IS the pair, so no grouping step can be got wrong
partition.why_not_random_or_hash: `random` is stateful so the assignment would depend on call order; `hash()` is per-process randomised so the partition would not be reproducible from (fraction, seed) alone

qualifications_carried_forward: EXPLORATORY. Snapshot B is our already-inspected 202609 and the M8/M9 results were produced from it, so any score obtained under this contract is exploratory whatever it shows.
PROVISIONAL POOLING. Whether Ki may be pooled across assay contexts at all is M5's open question; every count here assumes the current pooling rule.
The confirmatory §7(A) attestation is NOT signed and this contract does not sign it.
scope: EXECUTABLE SPECIFICATION, NOT EXECUTED. Nothing fitted, no prediction metric computed, no downloads, no docking, confirmatory freeze unsigned.

measured_difference.note: the contract forbids assuming this difference is zero, so it is measured. A-present means the pair has KI evidence in snapshot A; fitted means it was supplied to model fitting.

strata.status: PLANNED fitting inputs. Nothing has been fitted, so these are the pairs the model-facing loaders WOULD emit, not pairs any model has seen.

subgroups.new_a_present_excluded_from_fitting: A evidence exists, the pair is in the train partition, and its A reading gives no usable label
subgroups.new_absent_from_a: no KI evidence in snapshot A at all
subgroups.new_reserved_for_validation: A evidence exists and the pair was reserved for validation

strata.validation_exposure: A pair reserved for validation is NOT untouched by model selection. Its A evidence is what the declared checkpoint-selection rule reads, so the selected checkpoint is a function of it. The pair is new to *fitting* and exposed to *selection*, and a result on it is weaker evidence than a result on a pair absent from A entirely.

worked_examples_versus_population_counts.distinction: `matching_pairs_in_audit` counts how many corpus pairs satisfy a pattern's PREDICATE -- a population count. The `real_example` beside it is ONE pair, shown so the predicate can be checked by hand against the archived bytes. A traceable example shows the pattern occurs and that the implementation handles it; it is not evidence about the population, and the cohort figures are measured separately rather than extrapolated from any example.
worked_examples_versus_population_counts.example_a_caveat: example (a) is absent from the audit by construction, not by rarity. That is a statement about what the audit emits, not a population count.
